correctness.rationale: For each facet edge, the intrinsic distance denominator is exactly the norm of the coordinate functional on the affine tangent space, which is the cycle-space projection norm. The orthogonal cut-space projector gives its square as one minus edge effective resistance. A radius-t ball is therefore feasible exactly when the corresponding facet-edge lower bounds are feasible. For a DAG, Farkas duality plus layer-cake decomposition of monotone potentials proves that nonnegative-flow feasibility is equivalent to lower-ideal cut inequalities. Substitution yields the minimum ratio and the complete center set. The proof explicitly excludes nonfacet coordinates from the distance constraints; a small transitive-triangle example verifies why this distinction is necessary.

value.rationale: The theorem converts a continuous intrinsic metric invariant of a broad class of lattice polytopes into a finite directed-cut optimization with graph-electrical weights. It exposes a structural link between flow-polytope geometry, cycle-space leverage, and order-ideal feasibility; it also gives every Chebyshev center, not only the radius. The transportation formula becomes one symmetric special case, while arbitrary DAGs exhibit genuinely nonconstant weights and larger controlling ideals.
